title: Flatten nested records to CSV
prompt:
People keep asking for our audit events as a spreadsheet. Please add `records_to_csv(records)` to csvexport.py. It takes a list of dicts (as returned by `loader.parse_ndjson`) and returns CSV text.

Columns:
- Nested dicts are flattened into dot-separated column names at any depth: `{"user": {"name": "ada"}}` gives a column `user.name`. A nested empty dict contributes no column.
- Column order is first-seen order: walk the records in order and each record's keys in insertion order (descending into nested dicts where they appear), adding a column the first time its name is seen.
- If two keys in the same record flatten to the same column name (e.g. a key `"a.b"` and `{"a": {"b": ...}}`), raise ValueError. A key that is a plain value in one record and a dict in another is fine: you just get both `a` and `a.b` columns.

Cells:
- `None` becomes an empty cell, `True`/`False` become `true`/`false`, any other scalar uses `str()`.
- Lists and tuples are joined with `;`, each item converted with the same scalar rules (so `[True, None, 2]` is `true;;2` and `[]` is an empty cell).
- A record that lacks a column gets an empty cell.

Output: a header row, then one row per record, written with the csv module's default dialect like the existing `rows_to_csv` (`\r\n` line endings, fields quoted only when needed, quotes doubled). An empty list of records returns `""`. Any record that isn't a dict raises TypeError. The input must not be modified.
acceptance: Exact output for flat records; dot paths at depth; first-seen column order across records with missing cells empty; list/tuple joining with ;; None/bool conversion including inside lists; quoting of commas, quotes and newlines; empty nested dict adds no column; scalar vs dict under the same key across records; empty input; ValueError on a within-record collision; TypeError for non-dict records; input unchanged.
difficulty_rationale: One function but several interacting rules (ordering across records, flattening, collisions, value conversion, CSV quoting).
